description: Sonnet rubric over story angles generated from the trust-drivers brief (E-1 / D-046)
brief_title: Brand trust drivers across urban Indian categories
brief_content: We are designing the 2026 brand trust syndicated study refresh. Objective: identify the dominant brand trust drivers across urban Indian categories, segment consumers by their trust profile, and map the differences in trust drivers across age cohorts. Audience: brand strategy and marketing teams across personal care, packaged foods, and small appliances.

accepted_hypotheses.statement: Among urban Gen-Z consumers, ingredient transparency on personal-care SKUs predicts purchase intent more strongly than brand heritage.
accepted_hypotheses.expected_direction: Gen-Z respondents will rank ingredient lists above brand heritage when ranking trust drivers.
accepted_hypotheses.confirmation_criteria: Maxdiff on trust drivers shows ingredient transparency in top-2 for Gen-Z but outside top-5 for Gen-X.

accepted_hypotheses.statement: Trust drivers in small appliances are dominated by warranty length and after-sales service, with brand-level affinity playing a minor role.
accepted_hypotheses.expected_direction: Conjoint utilities for warranty and service exceed brand-level utility in small appliances.
accepted_hypotheses.confirmation_criteria: Choice-based conjoint shows warranty + service utilities >2× brand utility.

accepted_personas.name: Gen-Z Label Scanner
accepted_personas.description: 21-year-old Bangalore software engineer who scans ingredient lists on every personal-care purchase.
accepted_personas.under_represents: Older urban Indian consumers, rural shoppers, men, lower-income households

hypothesis_verdicts.summary: Gen-Z maxdiff ranked ingredient transparency #1; Gen-X ranked it #6.

emergent_patterns.pattern: Gen-Z treats certifications as table-stakes, not differentiators
emergent_patterns.description: Gen-Z respondents flagged certifications as 'expected', not as positive signals.
emergent_patterns.why_interesting: The trust-shortcut value of certifications is eroding fastest in the youngest cohort.

caveats: Sample skewed urban metros only — no tier-2/3 representation.

accepted_recommendation.insight: In personal care, ingredient transparency has replaced brand heritage as the dominant Gen-Z trust shortcut, while certifications have collapsed into table-stakes.
accepted_recommendation.recommended_action: Redesign personal-care packaging to lead with full ingredient disclosure and active-ingredient call-outs ahead of brand mark by Q3 2026.
caveats: Urban-metros only — tier-2/3 buying behaviour not yet observed.
Personal-care category-specific — does not apply to packaged foods or appliances.
